page: Amazon Web Services m8id.24xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The instance is equipped with 384 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage consists of 5700 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and network connectivity is supported by a 40 Gbps baseline bandwidth managed via the Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier status in multi-core Geekbench scores, Passmark CPU tests, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, while single-core CPU performance falls in the average to strong categories. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching top-tier levels for read-only operations on both small and large blocks. In database and application workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier throughput for Redis SET operations, static web serving, and Passmark database operations.

A key performance tradeoff is visible in LLM inference workloads: while prompt processing speeds for small, medium, and large models rank in the top tier, text generation speeds drop to average levels for small and large models. The hardware configuration, combining high-speed DDR5 memory, a large 480 MB L3 cache, and 5.7 TB of local NVMe storage, makes this instance suitable for database hosting, software compilation, and data-intensive general-purpose workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services m8id.24xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. It includes 384 GB of DDR5 memory and 5700 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, operating on the Nitro hypervisor with a 40 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results place this instance in the top tier for multi-core processing, memory read bandwidth, and database operations, though single-core performance remains average. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, which accelerate matrix and vector operations. While prompt processing for LLM inference ranks in the top tier, text generation speeds are more moderate. This resource profile is suited for database workloads, multi-threaded software compilation, and high-throughput web serving.
